prose_updates.tldr: A balanced pilot and a positive-support exact-\(\alpha\) main-wave mixture retain exact Horvitz--Thompson centering for the realized finite-population factorial vector.  The proved contribution includes the exact two-component risk identity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain limit, and first-order Gaussian optimality of the empirical oracle against arbitrary exact finite-score actions.  The two branches of the endpoint lemma exclude both a fixed positive pilot fraction with a nonvanishing main wave and a sublinear main wave.  The balanced-grid argmin proposition remains purely deterministic: compact-window second-order convergence, the pilot-information bridge, and three endpoint comparisons remain open, so no square-root pilot recommendation is yet certified.

project_justification.gap: Existing factorial rerandomization theory supplies first-order Gaussian precision and existing two-wave work supplies accounting architecture, but neither proves the moving-boundary exact Horvitz--Thompson comparison at the square-root pilot scale.  The present information audit also shows that the stated moment conditions do not identify the pilot Fisher-information limit.
project_justification.niche: On a fixed complete baseline array with a full-dimensional product parameter domain, the design problem separates exactly into a deletion contrast and a potentially signed action-loss contrast.  A compactness, leave-one-unit, and Gaussian lower-tail argument controls the latter at first order for arbitrary actions, while the uniform deletion identity handles nonconvergent pilot fractions whenever the main wave diverges.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact pooled Horvitz--Thompson accounting, the explicit first-order exact-mixture oracle-gain coefficient, first-order arbitrary-action Gaussian optimality, both branches of the macroscopic endpoint exclusion, the exact pilot likelihood and realized information audit, and a conditional deterministic argmin certificate.  It leaves both frontier coefficients, compact-window convergence, the information-to-action bridge, and the three remaining endpoint comparisons as explicit open questions.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Deng provide the closest factorial sample-splitting architecture and first-order oracle equivalence; their results inform the present first-order comparison but do not supply the deletion cancellation or exact moving-boundary action loss.  Li and Ding provide the random-partition central limit theorem used for bounded conditional-mean tables.  Li, Ding, and Rubin provide the symmetric truncated-Gaussian predecessor, while the present first-order arbitrary-action comparison additionally carries randomized ties, exact unequal inclusions, and arbitrary centered quadratic actions through a subsequence limit.  Yamin provides the deterministic compact-localization and argmin-transfer architecture, not the statistical square-root rate or its coefficients.  Armstrong's LAN efficiency bounds become relevant only after an actual pilot-information limit is available.  Horvitz and Thompson support exact inverse-inclusion centering.  Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella motivate sequential factorial replications, but no pilot-size recommendation is certified until the compact-window and three remaining endpoint premises are proved.
prose_updates.interpretation: For planning, the proved coefficient \(a(\beta)\) quantifies the first-order loss from deleting a macroscopic fraction of units for learning.  No exact finite quadratic action can asymptotically beat the empirical Gaussian oracle at order \(N^{-1}\), even though finite-lattice action-loss contrasts may be negative.  Consequently, the second branch of the endpoint lemma rules out pilot and main waves that both retain positive fractions, while its first branch rules out a sublinear main wave.  The familiar balance \(A t+B/t\) remains a conditional design calculation, not a validated sample-size rule for this experiment.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Exact score orderings can jump on deterministic lattices and exact inclusion probabilities can be unequal.  Compact action and parameter subsequences, zero Gaussian boundary mass, an explicit leave-one-unit coupling, and exact residual cancellation absorb those effects at first order and suffice for both macroscopic endpoint branches.  They provide no quantitative remainder at scale \(n^{-3/2}\), so they do not establish the compact-window second-order premise or the three remaining endpoint comparisons.  Separately, smooth first and second outcome moments do not control score information as a function of the baseline, so the pilot LAN information cannot be fixed at \(I(\beta)\) without additional derivation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are exact Horvitz--Thompson centering and accounting, the one-wave risk bound, common oracle-map convergence, Gaussian boundary regularity, the first-order exact-mixture oracle gain, first-order arbitrary-action Gaussian optimality, the exact pilot likelihood and information audit, exclusion of positive pilot fractions and sublinear main waves through the two branches of one endpoint lemma, and the conditional deterministic envelope transfer.  The coefficient \(A\) remains an unresolved deletion candidate and \(B\) remains a Gaussian action candidate.  Uniform frontier-scale deletion, exact finite action curvature, information convergence, bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), the window \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\), and the unconditional global pilot rule are open.  The causal estimand remains the fixed realized factorial vector throughout.

statement_notes.justification: The first branch excludes a sublinear main wave, and the second excludes pilot and main waves that both retain positive fractions.
statement_notes.gap: Only bounded pilots, diverging pilots with \(m=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(\sqrt n=o(m)=o(n)\) remain open.
statement_notes.consumer: The two macroscopic endpoint exclusions needed by the conditional grid transfer are handled by the two branches of this lemma.
